body:
cc @Nodragem 

> +++ In addition, I can no longer remove pieces by left-clicking on them, which is a regression, causing slowness in the process of drawing and removing pieces.

In which scenarios were tiles removable with the left click? This should only happen if using the Erase tool. Otherwise, only the right click should remove tiles.

> cc [@Nodragem](https://github.com/Nodragem)
> 
> > +++ In addition, I can no longer remove pieces by left-clicking on them, which is a regression, causing slowness in the process of drawing and removing pieces.
> 
> In which scenarios were tiles removable with the left click? This should only happen if using the Erase tool. Otherwise, only the right click should remove tiles.

@Calinou 

In Godot 4.3 there is no eraser tool - tiles were removed with the left mouse click.

I noticed that now the left click is used to move in scene, which is excellent but a regression in relation to the speed with which pieces are placed/removed.

Is it possible to remap this function? With the middle mouse click for example?

Are you using a left-handed mouse (with inverted buttons)? I've never seen tiles being deleted by left-clicking, unless you selected an eraser tool beforehand.

Left-clicking also does not trigger freelook or orbiting by default. If it does, check your editor settings (specifically **3D > Navigation Scheme**) and reset them to the default.

> Is it possible to remap this function? With the middle mouse click for example?

Middle mouse panning is used for orbit, so this wouldn't make sense.
